text.system: You score free-text answers from an FSU undergraduate's research-lab matching survey. From the text alone, rate the student's interest on four axes: computational (modeling, simulation, analyzing neural data, AI), cognitive (behavior, decision-making, memory, perception in people), organism (hands-on work with animals or tissue), clinical (disorders and their treatment). Use 1-5 (1 none, 3 moderate, 5 central to what they wrote) or null when the text gives no evidence either way. Never infer from absence: a text about human memory says nothing about animals, so organism is null, not 1. Add 1-5 short topic tags (e.g. 'working memory', 'sleep', 'BCI') and quote the phrase that most drove your scores.

questions.notes: Structured answers feed the statistical classifier directly. free_text answers are scored by Haiku into the same feature space at match time. Nothing from the transcript field is stored; it is parsed client-side into course codes and titles only. Wording rules (v0.2): plain words, one idea per question, neutral answer choices (neither end of a scale sounds better), and supportive framing ("Not yet", "Not sure yet"). Option keys are the stored values and must not change; labels, prompts, help and intro text can. help = one optional line under a prompt.

classifier_targets.axis_computational: 1-5: interest in how neurons/circuits compute, modeling, data analysis
classifier_targets.axis_cognitive: 1-5: interest in behavior, decision-making, memory, perception in people
classifier_targets.axis_organism: 1-5: interest in / comfort with animal models and wet-lab work
classifier_targets.axis_clinical: 1-5: interest in disorders, treatment, clinical relevance
classifier_targets.organism_comfort: subset of [human, rodent, other_vertebrate, invertebrate, in_silico_only]
classifier_targets.career_goal: one of [phd, md, md_phd, industry_ml, industry_other, undecided]
classifier_targets.project_length: one of [dis_one_semester, dis_multi_semester, honors_thesis, urop, volunteer_first]

options.label: How brain cells work together to process information
How people think, decide, remember, and perceive

Building AI that learns the way brains do

rows.label: Building computer models or analyzing data
Studying how people think, decide, remember, and perceive
Hands-on work with animals or tissue samples
Brain and mental health conditions and their treatment

questions.help: One or two sentences is plenty. A rough idea is fine.

What would you be comfortable working with?

labs.name: Dewan Lab

labs.bridge: The one Scientific Computing faculty member whose department page explicitly lists computational neuroscience, so a CS/math student can do fMRI classification or cortical-network stability work without leaving a computing department.

labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; profile lists the lab as accepting graduate students and names two current graduate students.
labs.bridge: Fly neurogenetics with high-throughput behavioral readouts (sleep, feeding) is a common first lab for biology students who later move into quantitative behavior analysis and circuit modeling.

labs.name: Arbeitman Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine
labs.focus: How complex behaviors are specified at the molecular-genetic level, focusing on mechanisms that create sex differences in the nervous system and underlie male and female reproductive behaviors.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; profile says the lab is accepting graduate students.
labs.bridge: Explicitly lists computational methods alongside wet-lab genomics, so a biology student can gain both fly neurogenetics and data-analysis experience in one lab.

labs.name: Kabbaj Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine
labs.focus: Neurobiology of individual and sex differences in depression and drug addiction, and epigenetic mechanisms of social bonding in prairie voles.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; lab page lists lab phone (850) 644-4930 and names graduate students, a research faculty member, and a lab assistant but no undergraduates.
labs.bridge: Behavioral neuroscience with a full molecular toolkit; best for biology or pre-health students who want stress/addiction neurobiology before any modeling.
labs.entry_point: Duclot, Lindsay, Koutakis, Wang & Kabbaj 2022, Biological Psychiatry (listed on lab page without DOI).

labs.name: Bhide Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine (Center for Brain Repair)
labs.focus: Developmental neurobiology centered on dopamine's role in brain development, linked to ADHD, early-onset torsion dystonia, and neurocognitive effects of pre- and early postnatal drug exposure.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; profile says accepting graduate students and links a College of Medicine directory page.
labs.bridge: Neurodevelopment and dopamine are foundational for later work on reinforcement-learning models; serves biology and pre-health students directly.

labs.name: Kumar Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine
labs.focus: Synaptic physiology of neocortical function and plasticity, focusing on AMPA and NMDA glutamate receptors and the ictogenic cells and circuits of the parahippocampal region in temporal lobe epilepsy.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; profile states not accepting graduate students and links a College of Medicine directory page.
labs.bridge: Electrophysiology and receptor kinetics are the raw material of biophysical neuron models; a biology student who learns patch-clamp here is well placed for Hodgkin-Huxley-style modeling later.

labs.name: Y. Wang Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine
labs.focus: How the binaural circuit of the auditory brainstem forms, functions, and breaks down, focusing on the fragile X protein FMRP in chickens, mice, gerbils, and postmortem human brain tissue.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; lab site https://med.fsu.edu/wangyuanlab/home has a Lab Members page not read here (needs confirmation).
labs.bridge: The auditory brainstem binaural circuit is one of the best-modeled circuits in neuroscience (sound localization), so anatomical and developmental data from this lab connect directly to classic comp-neuro models.

labs.name: Zhou Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine
labs.focus: Developing and characterizing transgenic mouse models of schizophrenia and studying its neurobiology at the molecular, synaptic, and neural-circuit levels, including regulation of neuronal ion channels.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; profile states not accepting graduate students and lists zhou@neuro.fsu.edu.
labs.bridge: Ion-channel regulation and synaptic deficits in a disease model give a biology or pre-health student the cellular electrophysiology grounding that circuit models of psychiatric disease assume.

labs.name: Megraw Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine (Center for Brain Repair)
labs.focus: Centrosome and cilia function in cell division, development, and disease, including the MCPH primary-microcephaly proteins framed as a neural stem cell disease.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; profile links lab site https://med.fsu.edu/megrawLab/home and lists the course BMS4932 Current Research in Biomedical Sciences.
labs.bridge: A cell-biology lab for biology students interested in neurodevelopment (microcephaly, neural stem cells) rather than circuits; teaches Drosophila and imaging skills transferable to any neuro lab.
labs.entry_point: Zheng et al. 2020, Nature Cell Biology, on centrosome protein function.

labs.name: Li Lab
labs.dept: Department of Chemistry & Biochemistry / Institute of Molecular Biophysics
labs.focus: Atomic-level structure and mechanism of large molecular assemblies in gene expression, emphasizing RNA:protein, RNA:RNA, and protein:protein interactions.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; lab site has a people directory and contact page only.
labs.bridge: Not a neuroscience lab; it is the confirmed structural-biology entry point for a strictly-chemistry undergraduate who wants biomolecular structure skills before moving toward channel/receptor or neurodegeneration work.

labs.name: Bleiholder Lab
labs.dept: Department of Chemistry & Biochemistry
labs.focus: Builds ion mobility/mass spectrometry instruments and companion computational methods, then uses them to probe the structure and dynamics of proteins and other biological systems.
labs.how_to_apply: Email Dr. Bleiholder at bleiholder@chem.fsu.edu for more information.
labs.bridge: Open to students from any area of chemistry, biochemistry or biophysics who want to pair instrument-based protein analysis with computational methods.
labs.entry_point: Tandem-TIMS, the lab's tandem-trapped ion mobility spectrometry technique, introduced in the November 2026 FSU News article about it.

labs.name: DuVal Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biological Science (Ecology & Evolution)
labs.focus: Investigates cooperation, mate choice and sexual selection in birds through a long-running study of lance-tailed manakins.
labs.how_to_apply: Email Dr. DuVal to ask whether undergraduate research positions are available.
labs.bridge: Fits upper-level students drawn to animal behavior and evolution who want an independent project for credit or honors.
labs.expectations: Undergraduate researchers join lab meetings and present their work there.
labs.entry_point: The lab's ongoing lance-tailed manakin mate choice and cooperation project, outlined on its Research page.

labs.name: Breithaupt Lab
labs.dept: Coastal & Marine Laboratory (Department of Biological Science faculty directory: Ecology & Evolution)
labs.focus: Examines the biogeochemistry of coastal ecosystems such as wetlands, oyster reefs and shorelines, including how their soils store carbon and nutrients and respond to change.
labs.bridge: Gives biology and environmental science majors field and lab experience in coastal soil science and nutrient cycling, based at the Coastal & Marine Laboratory.
labs.entry_point: The lab's ecosystem-health work for the Apalachicola Bay System Initiative (ABSI), listed on its Research page.

labs.name: Stroupe Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biological Science / Institute of Molecular Biophysics
labs.focus: Works out the structures and mechanisms of protein complexes behind bacterial sulfur metabolism, chiefly sulfite reductase, alongside work on ribosome biogenesis.
labs.bridge: Offers biology and biochemistry students bench experience in protein biochemistry and structure-determination methods such as crystallography and cryo-EM.
labs.entry_point: Murray, Weiss, Stanley, Nagy & Stroupe's small-angle neutron scattering paper on NADPH-dependent sulfite reductase, highlighted on the department's Cell & Molecular Biology research page.

labs.name: Rams Lab
labs.dept: National High Magnetic Field Laboratory (MagLab) / Chemical and Biomedical Engineering, FAMU-FSU College of Engineering
labs.focus: Studies the structure, dynamics, and function of macromolecules, especially membrane-associated peptides and proteins.
labs.how_to_apply: Email Professor Ramamoorthy (aramamoorthy@fsu.edu) with your CV, previous research experience, and your motivation for applying.
labs.bridge: Recruits undergraduates from engineering, physics, chemistry, biology and neuroscience, and its amyloid and Alzheimer's-related projects connect structural biophysics to brain disease.

labs.name: Sussman Lab
labs.dept: Mathematics, Arts and Sciences
labs.focus: Simulates multiphase flows and uses AI and data fitting to speed up those simulations and to predict hurricane strength from sea surface temperature data.
labs.how_to_apply: Listed in the FSU UROP project database with msussman@fsu.edu as the contact email.
labs.bridge: Open to all majors with no prerequisites, so it suits students who want to build programming and applied-math skills through simulation and data-fitting projects.
labs.expectations: About 7.5 hours per week on a flexible schedule, fully remote, doing programming, mathematics and writing (e.g. the poster).
labs.entry_point: The UROP project "Using AI to accelerate multiphase flow predictions" is the listed starting project.

labs.name: Tropical Paleo-Dynamics Group
labs.dept: Department of Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Science (EOAS)
labs.focus: Reconstructs past tropical Pacific climate from the stable isotope and trace element geochemistry of corals and lake sediments, combined with theory and models.
labs.bridge: Undergraduates from majors as varied as Geology, Environmental Science and Neuroscience have joined through UROP or WIMSE and worked with graduate mentors on coral geochemistry, making it a good first lab for students interested in climate and Earth science.
labs.entry_point: Rodriguez et al. (2025), "A coral diagenesis and physiology framework for improving coral δ18O paleoclimate reconstructions," Paleoceanography and Paleoclimatology.

labs.name: MakeX Lab
labs.dept: FSU Computer Science
labs.focus: Embeds sensing and computation into textiles, furniture and everyday materials, and builds tools that make those technologies accessible (human-computer interaction and physical AI).
labs.how_to_apply: Email the lab (twu@cs.fsu.edu) with your CV and one or two project ideas you would be excited to explore.
labs.bridge: Suits students who want hands-on building that mixes computer science with engineering, materials, design and health, in a lab that lists undergraduate students on its team.
labs.expectations: The lab looks for people who are self-motivated, collaborative, and persistent when navigating the uncertainty of research.
labs.entry_point: Textro (UIST 2026), a solderless and chipless toolkit for creating, fabricating and testing smart textile interfaces.

labs.name: Queen of the Sciences Lab
labs.dept: Department of Psychology (Cognition and Cog Neuro / Developmental)
labs.focus: Studies logical reasoning and mathematical thinking in children and adults, and how these skills are learned and develop, with the aim of improving math education.
labs.how_to_apply: Email a cover letter, resume/CV, unofficial transcript and any other relevant information to David Braithwaite (dbraithwaite@fsu.edu); applicants are contacted for an interview after review.
labs.bridge: A cognitive-science lab pairing behavioral studies with computational modeling, useful for students who want a route into modeling human learning without wet-lab or imaging work.
labs.expectations: DIS students must be sophomores or higher with a 3.2+ GPA and commit 3 credits (9 hours) per week for at least two consecutive semesters; face-to-face and remote options exist.
labs.entry_point: Braithwaite & Siegler (2024), "A Unified Model of Arithmetic With Whole Numbers, Fractions, and Decimals," Psychological Review.

labs.name: Spector Lab
labs.dept: Department of Psychology / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: Studies the neural basis of taste and how taste guides feeding and drinking, using rodent models.
labs.how_to_apply: Contact Dr. Spector (spector@psy.fsu.edu) for an assessment of fit and availability.
labs.expectations: Commit at least two semesters, attend lab meetings and help lab personnel with experiments; a strong biology background is preferred.
labs.entry_point: Current project on changes in taste function and ingestive behavior associated with gastric bypass surgery.

labs.name: Motor Speech Lab
labs.dept: School of Communication Science and Disorders, College of Communication and Information
labs.focus: Investigates speech impairments in people with movement disorders such as Parkinson's disease and how those impairments reduce speech intelligibility.
labs.how_to_apply: Fill out the short interest form linked from the lab's home page.
labs.bridge: Gives students headed toward speech-language pathology or speech science hands-on experience with instrumented speech measurement in clinical populations.
labs.entry_point: Ongoing project tracking articulatory movements with EMA in speakers with dysarthria and L2 speakers of English.

labs.name: Cougle Lab
labs.dept: Department of Psychology (Clinical)
labs.focus: Works on understanding and treating anxiety disorders, problematic anger, and obsessive-compulsive and related disorders, including technology-based treatments.
labs.how_to_apply: Email the lab at couglelabras@gmail.com; for a Summer or Fall start, do so at least one month before Spring semester ends.
labs.bridge: Suits students who want clinical research experience with anxiety and related disorders ahead of graduate school.
labs.expectations: Minimum 3.5 GPA and a 9-hour-per-week commitment for two semesters.
labs.entry_point: "Text message safety behavior reduction for social anxiety: A randomized controlled trial," listed on Cougle's faculty page.

labs.name: Gerend Health Psychology Lab
labs.dept: Department of Behavioral Sciences and Social Medicine, College of Medicine
labs.focus: Studies the social and psychological factors behind health and health behavior and designs behavior-change interventions, with an emphasis on reducing health disparities.
labs.how_to_apply: Email Mary Gerend, Ph.D. (mary.gerend@med.fsu.edu) for more information; instructor permission is required to sign up for DIS.
labs.bridge: Suits students heading to medical school or to graduate study in health psychology or public health who want participant-facing behavioral research experience.
labs.expectations: Minimum 3.2 GPA, 9 hours per week (3 credits) and the weekly Tuesday 3:30-4:30 PM lab meeting, with duties such as running experimental sessions, recruiting participants and coding qualitative data.
labs.entry_point: Current projects cover discrimination and health, cancer prevention behavior, and health messaging, and the lab page links Dr. Gerend's publication bibliography.

labs.name: Flynn Lab: Behavioral Health Research and Community Engagement Program
labs.dept: Department of Behavioral Sciences and Social Medicine, College of Medicine (Center for Behavioral Health Integration)
labs.focus: Works on detecting, treating and preventing mental health disorders, especially depression in women around childbearing, through clinic- and community-based research.
labs.how_to_apply: Complete the lab application form linked under DIS Opportunities on the lab page; questions go to FSUCBHI@med.fsu.edu.
labs.bridge: Gives psychology and pre-health students clinic- and community-facing behavioral health research experience, with a shot at a presentation or publication after two or more semesters.
labs.expectations: 3.2 GPA or higher, sophomore standing or above, reliable transportation, Abnormal Psychology and Research Methods completed, a preferred two-semester commitment at 2+ credits, and a weekly one-hour lab meeting.
labs.entry_point: Mulligan, Flynn & Hajcak (2019), "Neural Response to Reward and Psychosocial Risk Factors Independently Predict Antenatal Depressive Symptoms", Biological Psychology.

labs.name: Development, Environment, and Resilience (DEaR) Lab
labs.dept: Department of Behavioral Sciences and Social Medicine, College of Medicine
labs.focus: Examines how biological and environmental factors shape neurobehavioral development and resilience in underrepresented groups, particularly people with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1).
labs.how_to_apply: Email the DIS instructor, Dr. Yang Hou (yang.hou@med.fsu.edu), for details; instructor permission is required to sign up.
labs.bridge: A fit for psychology and pre-health students who want training in quantitative developmental and clinical science (statistical modeling, meta-analysis, open-science practice) applied to a neurodevelopmental genetic condition.
labs.entry_point: The lab's Review-NF1 project, a set of systematic reviews and meta-analyses on neurobehavioral function in NF1.

labs.name: Guan Lab
labs.dept: Department of Chemical & Biomedical Engineering, FAMU-FSU College of Engineering
labs.focus: Engineers micro- and nanoparticles for drug delivery, biosensing and the study of phagocytosis.
labs.how_to_apply: Contact the Department of Chemical & Biomedical Engineering about Undergraduate Research Program (URP) requirements; you must be approved and enrolled in URP before submitting the Honors in the Major application.
labs.bridge: Serves students interested in biomedical engineering for drug delivery and biosensing, with the PI listing dementia/Alzheimer's disease and cancer as content expertise.
labs.expectations: The department's URP is for juniors and seniors undertaking independent and original research.
labs.entry_point: FSU News story (2025-03-27) on the lab's microparticles for studying protein degradation and immune cell behavior.

labs.name: Resilient and Autonomous Systems Lab (RAS Lab)
labs.dept: Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering, FAMU-FSU College of Engineering
labs.focus: Develops resilient control and autonomous-systems methods for cyber-physical systems such as energy infrastructure and autonomous vehicles.
labs.bridge: Serves students interested in control systems, robotics and autonomous vehicles, and power-grid security; the lab's People page has an undergraduate section and lists undergraduate alumni.
labs.entry_point: The lab's Research page, which outlines its three areas (resilient control systems, autonomous systems control, power and energy systems) and links to selected projects.

labs.name: Fernández-Cabán Lab
labs.dept: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, FAMU-FSU College of Engineering (RIDER Center faculty)
labs.focus: Studies how extreme winds affect buildings and civil infrastructure, combining wind tunnel and field experiments with computational modeling and design optimization.
labs.how_to_apply: Reach out to the mentor using the contact in the project document (Dr. Pedro Fernández-Cabán, plfernandez@eng.famu.fsu.edu).
labs.bridge: Suits students who want machine learning, simulation and high-performance computing applied to hurricane and structural engineering; the CEE mentor flier lists him as open to undergraduates from civil or related fields.
labs.expectations: The Fall 2024 undergraduate project had the student extract wind tunnel data and run multi-fidelity computational wind simulations in RIDER's High-Performance Computer Lab.
labs.entry_point: College news story "Making Roofs More Hurricane-Proof Through Better Geometry" about his team's work on wind damage to low-rise roofs.

labs.name: Downes Lab
labs.pi: Rebekah Downes (lab site and college news use Rebekah Sweat)
labs.dept: Department of Industrial & Manufacturing Engineering, FAMU-FSU College of Engineering (High-Performance Materials Institute)
labs.focus: Develops and models composites and nanomaterials for extreme environments, using predictive simulation to speed up new material development.
labs.how_to_apply: The IME department says students interested in research should contact individual faculty members directly; the college profile lists downes@eng.famu.fsu.edu.
labs.bridge: Serves students interested in aerospace and extreme-environment materials who want hands-on composites work at the High-Performance Materials Institute alongside modeling.
labs.entry_point: "Supersonic hot jet ablative testing and analysis of boron nitride nanotube hybrid composites", a 2024 paper by the lab's doctoral students linked from the college news story.

labs.name: Social Development Lab
labs.dept: Human Development and Family Science
labs.focus: Studies how social anxiety and relationships with peers and family together shape children's and adolescents' social and emotional development, especially across transitions such as the move to middle school and into young adulthood.
labs.how_to_apply: Complete the application form linked under Opportunities on the lab page to join as a practicum student or volunteer.
labs.bridge: Serves students drawn to developmental psychology, child anxiety or family science who want experience on a long-running longitudinal study of human participants, with practicum and volunteer roles for undergraduates.
labs.entry_point: Gazelle & Wu (2026), "Co-development of anxious solitude and social anxiety symptoms from middle childhood through early adolescence," Child Psychiatry & Human Development.

labs.name: Cardiovascular and Applied Physiology (CAP) Laboratory
labs.dept: Department of Health, Nutrition, and Food Sciences, Anne Spencer Daves College of Education, Health, and Human Sciences
labs.focus: Human cardiovascular physiology research on modifiable health factors that could lower cardiovascular disease risk.
labs.how_to_apply: The team page sends prospective members to the openings section of the lab's contact page (caplaboratory.com/contact.html#openings).
labs.bridge: Hosts UROP students and undergraduate interns from majors as varied as nursing, psychology, biochemistry and public health, many of them on pre-health tracks.

labs.name: Ormsbee Lab at the Institute of Sports Sciences and Medicine (ISSM)
labs.dept: Department of Health, Nutrition, and Food Sciences / Institute of Sports Sciences and Medicine
labs.focus: Performance nutrition and exercise physiology in people, testing how nutritional interventions change metabolism, body composition and human performance.
labs.bridge: Suits exercise physiology, nutrition and pre-health students who want hands-on human performance and body-composition testing, since the institute offers students laboratory experiences and internships.
labs.entry_point: The ISSM page describes a current investigation into whether training on the AlterG antigravity treadmill can improve running performance.

labs.name: Brain, Learning, Attention, and Performance (BLAP) Lab
labs.dept: Sport Psychology, Department of Educational Psychology and Learning Systems
labs.focus: Studies the cognitive and motor processes behind skill learning, movement and expert performance, including how anxiety, attention and assistive technologies affect them.
labs.how_to_apply: The Sport Psychology Lab page names Dr. David Eccles as main supervisor for its DIS and gives Trey Wood (tjw24b@fsu.edu) as the lab contact.
labs.bridge: An option for students after motor-skill learning and human performance research, pairing EEG and eye tracking with sport and human-machine settings outside the neuroscience program.
labs.expectations: DIS students need 9 hours per week in the lab (3 credits), motivation to learn about sport and exercise research, and the ability to work in a team.
labs.entry_point: DeCouto, Bilalić & Williams (2024), "Neuroimaging and perceptual-cognitive expertise in sport: A narrative review of research and future directions," Neuropsychologia.

labs.name: FSU eHealth Lab
labs.dept: School of Information (iSchool)
labs.focus: Biomedical and health informatics: building eHealth tools for health education and patient self-management, and analysing electronic health data to improve health care and research.
labs.bridge: Gives students aiming at health, medicine or data science experience with machine learning and NLP on health data; past UROP undergraduates came from Biological Sciences and Computer Science.

labs.name: CLaSS Lab (Children's Literacy and Speech Sound Lab)
labs.dept: School of Communication Science & Disorders
labs.focus: Children's literacy and speech sounds (taken from the lab's full name; the student page gives no further description).
labs.how_to_apply: Complete CITI human-subjects training and send the certificate of completion to Dr. Farquharson at kfarquharson@fsu.edu.
labs.bridge: Suits students interested in communication science and disorders or children's literacy who want human-subjects research experience, starting from 3 volunteer hours a week with an honors-thesis route.
labs.expectations: Volunteers need at least 3 hours of availability per week and must finish CITI training before working in the lab.

labs.name: XS/FS Experimental Social Science Lab
labs.dept: Department of Economics (XS/FS Research Cluster with Political Science and Accounting)
labs.focus: Uses laboratory experiments to study how individuals and groups make choices, to inform policy in economics, political science and business.
labs.how_to_apply: The Economics undergraduate research page says to contact Dr. Ryvkin (dryvkin@fsu.edu) about assisting, while the lab's People page lists Luke Boosey (lboosey@fsu.edu) as Lab Director.
labs.bridge: Lets students interested in decision-making see paid human-subject experiments run outside psychology, with faculty from economics, political science and accounting.
labs.entry_point: Boosey, Brookins and Ryvkin (2020), "Information disclosure in contests with endogenous entry: An experiment", Management Science.

labs.name: Complementary Health Innovation Lab (CHIL)
labs.dept: College of Nursing (Brain Science and Symptom Management Center)
labs.focus: Develops and tests brief and intensive mindfulness-based and other mind-body interventions that can be embedded in medical care to reduce pain and improve quality of life.
labs.how_to_apply: The UROP listing gives Adam Hanley (adam.hanley@fsu.edu) as contact and Carter Minnick (cm25bo@fsu.edu) as research assistant supervisor.
labs.bridge: Patient-facing clinical research on pain and anxiety that suits pre-health and psychology students, with a UROP listing open to all majors.
labs.expectations: The UROP listing states about 8 hours a week during business hours, in person at an off-campus clinic, recruiting patients, guiding them through brief tablet-based interventions and managing study data.
labs.entry_point: Hanley et al. (2023), "The mindful warm-up: Proof of concept for a brief embedded intervention", listed on his College of Nursing page.

labs.name: Gnanasambandam Lab
labs.dept: Industrial & Manufacturing Engineering, FAMU-FSU College of Engineering
labs.focus: Builds physics-informed AI and scientific machine-learning methods to improve manufacturing, especially metal 3D printing, and AI tools for designing materials experiments.
labs.how_to_apply: His UROP listings give a contact email for prospective research assistants (rg24o@fsu.edu on the more recent listing).
labs.bridge: Applied machine-learning and software experience on engineering problems, with a UROP listing open to all majors.
labs.expectations: UROP listings state about 5 hours a week, partially remote, doing software development and meeting materials scientists to gather feedback.
labs.entry_point: The UROP project "User Friendly Software Development for AI-driven Materials Science", which builds software around the lab's existing AI methods for designing experiments.

labs.name: Solís Lab
labs.dept: Health, Nutrition, and Food Sciences, Anne Spencer Daves College of Education, Health, and Human Sciences
labs.focus: Studies how cardiac and skeletal muscle cells sense and adapt to mechanical load in health and in heart disease.
labs.how_to_apply: The UROP listing gives csolis@fsu.edu as the contact email for the project.
labs.bridge: Mixes muscle cell biology with hardware design and molecular modeling, so it serves engineering, physics and pre-health students interested in cardiovascular research.
labs.expectations: The UROP bioreactor listing states about 8 hours a week on a flexible, partially remote schedule, drawing up designs and building and testing prototypes.
labs.entry_point: Tigro et al. (2025), "Desensitization of the Cardiac Troponin Complex by TnI Phosphorylation and Epigallocatechin-3-Gallate", listed on his faculty page.

families.label: Computational
families.blurb: Code, models and data: the work happens on a computer.

families.label: Experimental
families.blurb: Bench, animals, instruments or field work: the work happens with your hands.

families.label: Human-centred
families.blurb: Participants, patients and behaviour: the work happens with people.

types.label: Computational neuroscientist
types.blurb: Code- and math-first: builds models of how brains, and the AI modeled on them, compute, and wants the model to be the work.

types.label: Computational biologist
types.blurb: Brings code and statistics to living systems: genes, cells and circuits, from sequencing data to animal models.

types.label: Neuroengineer
types.blurb: Wants to build things that read or write brain activity: signals, devices, closed loops.
jobs: Neurotech and medical device R&D engineer

types.label: Cognitive scientist
types.blurb: Studies how people think, decide, remember and perceive, with experiments on human participants.

types.label: Clinical researcher
types.blurb: Motivated by disorders and patients; wants research that could change how people are diagnosed or treated.

types.label: Experimental neuroscientist
types.blurb: Happiest at the bench: hands-on work with animals, tissue and circuits to see how brains really work.

axes.name: clinical interest + organism interest  vs  open problems (vs checklists) + computational interest
clinical interest + comfortable with human  vs  comfortable with invertebrate + comfortable with other vertebrate
mixed  vs  comfortable with invertebrate + comfortable with other vertebrate

lenses.label: Skills
lenses.help: Coding, math, and bench vs keyboard: could you do the day-to-day work now?

lenses.help: The four interest axes and the organisms you'd work with.

lenses.label: Goals
lenses.help: Project type, where you're headed after FSU, and how you like to work.
